policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'his disciples'; the possessive renders αὐτοῦ, which the omission reading lacks ('the disciples').
Pure word order within the infinitive clause; 'that occasions of stumbling should come' renders either sequence identically.
ASV 'but woe unto him' fits πλὴν οὐαί and οὐαὶ δέ alike; both are adversative connectives ASV renders 'but'.
ASV reads plain 'a millstone'. Where ASV renders μύλος ὀνικός it writes 'great millstone' (the donkey-turned stone); the unqualified noun answers to λίθος μυλικός.
Word order only; 'one of these little ones' renders either arrangement.
ASV reads 'if thy brother sin' with no 'against thee'; the RP reading's εἰς σέ is unrendered, and ASV supplies 'against thee' where it stands (v. 4).
Aorist subjunctive spelling variants of the same verb; 'if he sin against thee' renders both.
ASV writes 'in the day' only once, with the first 'seven times'; the second clause is bare 'and seven times turn again to thee', so the added τῆς ἡμέρας here is unrendered.
ASV reads 'turn again to thee'; 'to thee' renders πρὸς σέ, which the omission reading lacks.
ASV reads 'that will say unto him'; 'unto him' renders αὐτῷ, absent from the omission reading.
Word order of verb and object; 'Doth he thank' renders either.
ASV reads 'the servant', not 'that servant'; the demonstrative ἐκείνῳ of the RP reading is unrendered.
ASV ends the verse at 'the things that were commanded?' with no rendering of οὐ δοκῶ ('I think not').
ASV punctuates 'We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which it was our duty to do' with no causal or complementizing 'for/because' answering to ὅτι.

ASV text reads plural 'as they were on the way to Jerusalem'; the added αὐτόν forces the singular subject, which ASV carries only in the margin ('Or, as he was'), and that note is an alternative rendering.
Case of the noun after διά; ASV 'along the borders of' (margin 'through the midst of') does not show accusative against genitive, and the margin is an alternative rendering.
ASV reads 'there met him ten men'; the explicit object 'him' renders αὐτῷ, which the base reading lacks.
ASV reads bare 'who stood afar off'. ASV renders ἀνίστημι with the ingressive 'stood up'/'rose up'; unmarked 'stood' answers to ἔστησαν.
Orthographic variation of the negative before a vowel; 'Were not the ten cleansed?' renders either.
ASV reads 'Lo, here! or, There!' — a single 'Lo', attached to 'here'. The added Ἰδού before ἐκεῖ would give a second 'Lo' that ASV does not write.

ASV 'Lo, there! Lo, here!' has two 'Lo's, in the order there-then-here, with no 'or': this excludes the reading with ἤ ('or') and the reading that reverses to here-then-there. The two remaining candidates differ only in punctuation spacing, which no English can show.
Presence of the article with ἀστραπή; ASV 'the lightning' takes the English definite article either way.

ASV distinguishes the two prepositional phrases: 'out of the one part under the heaven' against 'unto the other part under heaven'. The article in the first answers to ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν, the anarthrous second to ὑπ' οὐρανόν.
ASV text reads 'in his day'; the mapped textual_variant note ('Some ancient authorities omit in his day') puts the omission in the margin, so the text carries the phrase.
Simple and compound forms of the same verb; ASV 'they were given in marriage' renders both.
πάντας and ἅπαντας are both 'them all'; the strengthened form is not distinguished in the English.
ASV 'Likewise even as it came to pass' fits καθώς and καὶ ὡς alike, 'even' answering to adverbial καί or absorbed into 'even as' for καθώς.
πάντας and ἅπαντας are both 'them all'; the strengthened form is not distinguished in the English.
ASV reads 'after the same manner', the identity adjective τὰ αὐτά; the demonstrative ταῦτα would give 'these things', which ASV does not write.
Presence of the article in the temporal phrase; ASV 'In that day' renders either.
ASV reads 'shall seek to gain his life'. 'Gain' answers to περιποιήσασθαι; σῶσαι is ASV's 'save', which it does not use here.
ASV reads 'but whosoever shall lose his life', the adversative δέ; the RP reading's καί would give 'and whosoever'.

ASV reads 'whosoever shall lose his life', not 'shall lose it': in this same verse ASV renders αὐτήν as 'it', so the added pronoun of the RP reading is excluded. Between the remaining subjunctive and future forms after the indefinite relative the English 'shall lose' does not distinguish.
Presence of the article with the numeral pair; ASV 'the one shall be taken' supplies the English article either way.
Word order of verb and numeral; 'There shall be two women grinding together' renders either.
Presence of the article; ASV 'the one shall be taken' supplies the English article either way.
ASV 'and the other shall be left' renders ἡ δέ and καὶ ἡ alike; ASV regularly gives connective δέ as 'and' in such paired clauses.
ASV has no verse 36 in the text; the mapped textual_variant note at v. 37 ('Some ancient authorities add verse 36 ...') puts the addition in the margin only.
ASV reads 'thither will the eagles also be gathered together'; 'also' renders καί, which the RP reading lacks.
